title: Packer and Ansible: building the sandbox image
bridge: A Packer image is like a Docker image for a whole VM. A recipe builds it once, and every VM starts from it. Except there are no layers and no cache, so a rebuild takes many minutes, and the image belongs to one region. Ansible writes the recipe's steps so that running them twice changes nothing the second time.
intro: Every sandbox starts from one image, ai-agent-sandbox. This lesson shows how it is made each night. Packer starts a VM, Ansible installs our tools on it, and Packer saves the disk as an AMI. A smoke test then decides whether the image is promoted, and rollback is one parameter.

p: A run could install Docker, Node and FCP Lab when it starts. It would wait many minutes for work that is the same every time. Baking does that work once a night, into the image.

G3-08 bakes the toolchain: Docker, Node 24, Python 3.13 and uv, git and jq. It also adds the agent user, the IMDS lock and spot-watch. G3-14 bakes the heavy part: a git mirror of fcp, npm and uv caches, and Playwright's browser. Then FCP Lab with fake seed data, a pinned Claude Code, and the nova-worker harness. One image serves all three sizes.
The image records what is in it in /etc/ai-agent-sandbox/manifest.json. freshenSandbox (G3-18) compares lockfile hashes with it and reinstalls only what changed.
sections.because: We write a manifest because the claim code and the PR receipt need to know exactly what each VM started from.

notes.text: Where main was when the image was built. A run fetches only the commits since.
If a run's lockfile hash matches, node_modules from the image are reused as they are.
The binary the harness runs through pathToClaudeCodeExecutable, so the smoke test proves the same one.

p: Packer reads a template in HCL. A source block says how to make the machine. Ours is amazon-ebs, which starts an EC2 VM and later saves its disk as an AMI. A build block lists sources and provisioners. A provisioner changes the machine; ours runs Ansible.

Our repo has one shared template, packer/packer/packer.pkr.hcl, for every image and both clouds. Each image adds packer/images/<image>/packer_vars.hcl and playbook.yml; each account adds packer/accounts/<account>/<cloud>-<region>.hcl. Below is the shape, not the real file.
sections.because: We read the template's shape first because build.sh and the vars files only make sense against it.

notes.text: Plugins are downloaded by packer init, like providers by tofu init.
The AMI name: rhino-ai-agent-sandbox-v1-testing-<time>. Testing images expire after 72 hours.
Find the newest image whose name matches, from the owner given.
Ansible runs over SSH against the build VM, with this image's playbook.

p: G3-08 adds packer/images/ai-agent-sandbox/packer_vars.hcl. It starts from our own base image, rhino-base-ubuntu-24, builds on a large VM for speed, and gives the disk 120 GiB.
Builds run in the inf account, inside the inf VPC, like every other image. Infrastructure PR #1724 (aws_ami_users) shares the AMIs with the ai-agents account, so its launch templates can use them.
sections.because: We build on m8i.2xlarge because build time is paid every night, and the build VM's size does not change the image.

code.file: packer/images/ai-agent-sandbox/packer_vars.hcl (sketch; copy variable names from a sibling image)
code.text:
image            = "ai-agent-sandbox"
source_ami_name  = "rhino-base-ubuntu-24-v1-release-*"
source_ami_owner = "self"
instance_type    = "m8i.2xlarge" # build speed; the same AMI runs lite, full and wide
volume_size      = 120

notes.text: Our hardened Ubuntu 24.04 base, itself built from Canonical's image.
self: the inf account that builds and owns these images.
GiB. Matches the launch templates' root disk.

sections.h: Ansible: tasks that describe a state
p: A playbook lists hosts and the roles to run on them. A role is a folder of tasks. A task calls a module, such as ansible.builtin.user, with the state you want: 'user agent exists with uid 1001'. If it already exists, the module changes nothing and reports ok; otherwise it acts and reports changed.

That property is idempotence: running the same playbook twice gives the same machine, and the second run reports changed=0. Below is the lab version of the role, three tasks taken from G3-08 and G3-09.
sections.because: We describe states instead of commands because a step that can run twice safely survives retries and reruns.

code.text:
---
- name: Create the non-root user the harness runs as
  ansible.builtin.user:
    name: agent
    uid: 1001
    shell: /bin/bash

- name: Send all web traffic through the egress proxy
  ansible.builtin.lineinfile:
    path: /etc/environment
    line: "{{ item }}"
  loop:
    - HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.ai-agents.example.com:3128
    - NO_PROXY=.amazonaws.com,.ai-agents.example.com

- name: Install the Spot interruption watcher
  ansible.builtin.copy:
    src: spot-watch.sh
    dest: /usr/local/bin/spot-watch
    mode: "0755"

notes.text: The module and the state. In the image it also joins the docker group (G3-08).
lineinfile adds the line only if it is missing, so reruns do not stack copies.
loop runs the task once per item. {{ item }} is Jinja, Ansible's template syntax.
NO_PROXY keeps AWS endpoints and our own services off the proxy (p4-5).
Copies files/spot-watch.sh from the role (p3-4). The image also adds its 5-second timer.

p: G3-14's bake_fcp.yml does the slow work. It clones a bare mirror of fcp with a short-lived token that exists only in the build job's environment. The work checkout borrows objects from the mirror. Then it fills the npm cache, installs Chromium for Playwright, builds FCP Lab's images and seeds fake data, and stops the lab.
creates: makes a command task idempotent: if that path exists, the task is skipped. become_user: agent runs a task as the agent user, so caches land in the right home folder.
sections.because: We pass the token through the environment, because a token written into git config would be baked into every VM.

code.text:
- name: Bare mirror of fcp (token from the build job, never written to disk)
  ansible.builtin.command: >-
    git -c credential.helper='!f() { echo username=x-access-token; echo "password=$GH_TOKEN"; }; f'
    clone --mirror https://github.com/RhinoHealth/fcp.git /var/cache/git/fcp.git
  environment: { GH_TOKEN: "{{ lookup('env', 'GH_BUILD_TOKEN') }}" }
  args: { creates: /var/cache/git/fcp.git }
- name: Work checkout that borrows objects from the mirror
  become_user: agent
  ansible.builtin.command: git clone --reference /var/cache/git/fcp.git /var/cache/git/fcp.git /work/fcp
  args: { creates: /work/fcp/.git }
- name: Fill the npm cache and install Playwright's Chromium
  become_user: agent
  ansible.builtin.shell: npm ci && npx playwright install chromium
  args: { chdir: /work/fcp/frontend }
- name: Build FCP Lab's images and seed its fake data, then stop it
  become_user: agent
  ansible.builtin.shell: |
    lab up --source /work/fcp --id sandbox --mode snapshot --refreshable
    lab status sandbox --json | jq -e '.state == "ready"'
    lab stop sandbox
  environment: { FCP_LAB_HOME: /var/lib/fcp-lab }

notes.text: A one-off credential helper that reads the token from the environment. Nothing is saved.
The token comes from the build job's env var. It never reaches the image.
Skip if the mirror exists: rerunning the role does not clone twice.
--reference shares objects with the mirror, so the checkout costs little disk.
jq -e fails the task unless the lab says ready. A broken lab never becomes an image.

p: G3-16 adds .github/workflows/build-ai-agent-sandbox.yml: a nightly cron at an odd minute, on infrastructure-runner-set, actions pinned by SHA. It builds on the testing channel, so an image never promoted expires after 72 hours.

The smoke job uses the OIDC role from G3-02. It launches one VM from the new AMI with the full launch template. Over SSM it runs nova-worker --version and one FCP Lab Playwright spec, not-found-page.spec.ts. The VM is always terminated, pass or fail. On a pass, the job promotes.
sections.because: We copy the current ID to -previous before writing the new one, so rollback never depends on remembering an AMI ID.

code.text:
prev=$(aws ssm get-parameter --name /ai-agents/sandbox/ami-id --query Parameter.Value --output text)
aws ssm put-parameter --name /ai-agents/sandbox/ami-id-previous --value "$prev" --overwrite
aws ssm put-parameter --name /ai-agents/sandbox/ami-id --value "$AMI" --overwrite
# then with the inf role, because inf owns the AMI:
aws ec2 disable-image-deprecation --image-id "$AMI"
aws ec2 create-tags --resources "$AMI" --tags Key=channel,Value=release

notes.text: The image VMs use today.
Kept one step back, for rollback.
From now on, every new VM boots the new image (resolve:ssm, p3-3).
A promoted image must not expire like a testing one.
packer_image_cleaner keeps the two newest release images, so only promoted images count.

sections.h: Rollback, and who presses the button
p: If the smoke test fails, nothing is promoted. The image stays on testing and expires in 72 hours, and the job posts the lab report to #ai-agents-alerts. If a promoted image turns out bad, rollback writes ami-id-previous back into ami-id.

Warm VMs still run the bad image until they are replaced. The sweeper recycles warm VMs older than 24 hours (p3-7), or a person terminates them at once. A person owns this workflow. Agents never dispatch workflows and never apply.
sections.because: We make rollback one parameter write because a broken image breaks every run at once, and the fix must take seconds.

code.text:
prev=$(aws ssm get-parameter --name /ai-agents/sandbox/ami-id-previous --query Parameter.Value --output text)
aws ssm put-parameter --name /ai-agents/sandbox/ami-id --value "$prev" --overwrite --output text
aws ssm get-parameter-history --name /ai-agents/sandbox/ami-id --query 'Parameters[].[Version,Value]' --output text

notes.text: The last good image.
New VMs boot it from now on.
The history shows every value the parameter had: a log of promotions and rollbacks.

quiz.q: Why is the AMI built on the testing channel first?

options.text: Testing images are cheaper to store
options.why: Storage cost is the same; the channel is about trust.

options.text: So an image that never passes the smoke test expires after 72 hours and never reaches a run
options.why: Only the smoke test's promote step moves it to release.

options.text: Because Packer cannot build release images directly
options.why: It could; we choose not to.

quiz.q: The second ansible-playbook run reports changed=0. What does that tell you?

options.text: The tasks are idempotent: the machine already matched every described state
options.why: That is the property that makes reruns and retries safe.

options.text: Ansible skipped the host because it ran recently
options.why: Ansible keeps no such memory; each task checked the state.
Failures show as failed=N and stop the play.

quiz.q: A promoted image breaks every run. What is the fastest safe fix?

options.text: Rebuild the image tonight with a fix
options.why: That leaves every run broken until tomorrow.

options.text: Edit the three launch templates to an older AMI ID
options.why: The templates read the parameter; editing them is slower and needs a Terraform apply.

options.text: Write ami-id-previous back into ami-id, then replace or wait out the warm VMs
options.why: New VMs boot the old image at once; warm VMs are recycled within a day, or terminated by hand.
